answer: Every applicant receives one brass heliograph mirror on its own ridge, its scratches photographed as its fingerprint. Each round the registry sets a fresh cadence; the holder flashes a signal toward the tower, where a falcon logs every flash. The next cadence grows from a kernel of the last flash's timing plus the holder's own seal, chaining flashes in order. Each additional identity needs a separate mirror and ridge: $310 to polish and mount, plus 16 ridge-days. Fielding 5,000 fakes costs $1.55 million and 80,000 ridge-days; one ridge holds one mirror, and sunlight cannot be split.
